overview: This 635-page file brings together U.S. diplomatic reporting, monitored Japanese broadcasts, and Board of Economic Warfare assessments of Japan’s economy in 1942–43. It traces wartime finance, production, food, labor, transport, and resource extraction across Japan and occupied Asia. Repeated analyses identify shipping and industrial processing as constraints on Japan’s ability to expand war production.
interest: Broadcast translations alongside U.S. assessments let historians compare Japanese economic claims with contemporary estimates of wartime capacity.
